---
engine: markdown
title: "Write values in their own notation"
subtitle: "Money, magnitudes, sizes, dates, and markup."
description: "Format a column as currency, scientific notation, byte sizes, dates, or Typst markup, and see which of them line up on a shared slot."
---

A price is not a number with a symbol stuck on it, and neither is a payload size.
Each formatter writes the value the way its notation is read, and the first three fill a slot the alignment stage reserves, so the columns line up on what matters: prices under their symbols, exponents under their multiplication signs, units under units.

```{typst}
//| file: ../../tests/visual/formatters.typ
//| echo: true
//| alt: "A bill of materials with prices carrying a euro sign at the left of the column and their decimals aligned, charges in scientific notation with the multiplication signs in a vertical line, and firmware sizes in bytes, kibibytes, mebibytes and gibibytes with the units aligned. Below it the same table with the yen symbol trailing each price, exponents written in e notation, and sizes in decimal prefixes."
```

The second table is the same figures said differently: `position: end` for the currencies written that way, `exponent: "e"` for output rather than typesetting, and `base: 1000` for the people who sell disks.
A yen figure carries no decimals, because the currency has no minor unit and two places would invent a precision it does not circulate in.

## Dates and markup

Neither produces alignment slots: a date has no separator to line up on, and a cell of markup is whatever it evaluates to, so both follow the column alignment like any other text.

```{typst}
//| file: ../../tests/visual/dates-markup.typ
//| echo: true
//| alt: "A release history table with versions, publication dates written as day, month name and year, and summaries in which some words are bold, some italic, and one is set in a monospaced face."
```

The three dates were written three different ways in the data: an ISO date, an ISO timestamp, and a `datetime` the document built.
The summaries are Typst markup carried as text, which is what a generator emits when a cell has emphasis it cannot express as content.
